questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: When a competent layer is stretched between incompetent rocks during deformation, what is the resulting pinch-and-swell structure called?
options: Pinch-and-swell structure formed in an incompetent layer squeezed between competent beds
Fold structure produced by vertical buckling of alternating competent and incompetent strata
Boudin (barrel-shaped) structure in competent layer stretched in incompetent matrix
A type of unconformity formed where competent beds are truncated by erosion at the surface
questions.solution: Boudinage: competent layer (quartzite) boudins in incompetent matrix (schist). Necking.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the mantle plume hypothesis, plumes are columns of hot material rising from where, and what do they drive?
options: Column of hot material rising from deep mantle (CMB). Drives hotspot volcanism
Surface-only phenomenon driven by plate motions, with no deep mantle involvement
Shallow origin in the crust, where radiogenic heat builds beneath thick continental shields
No evidence, as seismic tomography shows no vertical conduits anywhere in the mantle
questions.solution: Plume: deep origin (D″ layer). Hawaiian chain. Iceland. Reunion. Plume head → flood basalt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: X-ray diffraction identifies minerals by:
options: Unique crystal structure producing characteristic diffraction pattern
Chemical composition alone determines the diffraction pattern of the mineral
Colour and optical properties observed under ordinary visible light
Grain size of the powder and its packing density in the sample holder
questions.solution: XRD: Bragg law. Each mineral has unique d-spacings.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which metallogenic province of India is correctly matched with its characteristic metal?
options: Dharwar (Au), Kolar (Zn), Cuddapah (Cu), Bastar (Fe), Singhbhum (Mo), Khetri (U), Rajpura-Dariba (Mn)
questions.solution: Singhbhum: Cu-U-Fe (Precambrian). Khetri: Cu (Proterozoic). Kolar: Au (Archean greenstone).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the rubidium-strontium radiometric dating system, the radioactive parent 87Rb decays by beta emission to which daughter nuclide?
questions.solution: Rb-Sr dating: 87Rb → 87Sr. Half-life ~48.8 Ga. Used for igneous and metamorphic rocks. Isochron method.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic fluid: H₂O ± CO₂. In pelites, fluid is mainly:
options: H₂O (released from breakdown of hydrous minerals)
O₂ (released from oxidation of ferrous iron in oxides)
N₂ (released from breakdown of organic matter)
questions.solution: Metamorphic fluid: H₂O from muscovite, chlorite breakdown. CO₂ in marbles, calc-silicates.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Garnet porphyroblast with inclusion trail (Si/Se) indicates:
options: Timing of growth relative to deformation
Composition of the surrounding country rock
Rate of cooling following peak metamorphism
questions.solution: Inclusion trails: show garnet grew during folding. Rotational vs non-rotational help determine syn-kinematic growth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Law of faunal succession: fossils succeed each other in definite order.
options: Fossils of one kind always occur in rocks of the same colour in any basin
The oldest strata always contain the most advanced fossil types in a sequence
Distinct fossil assemblages can repeat at widely different levels in one section
Same fossil assemblage never recurs in different ages
questions.solution: William Smith: each formation has distinctive fossils. Index fossils for correlation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Desert pavement surfaces are formed primarily by which aeolian process?
options: Deflation removing fines, leaving lag gravel
Deposition of windblown silt and fine sand
Sheet flooding by ephemeral desert streams
Concentration of salts by capillary evaporation
questions.solution: Desert pavement: surface of closely packed stones. Wind removes fine particles (deflation), leaving coarse lag.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geophysical technique analyzes surface waves to determine shear wave velocity (Vs30)?
options: Multichannel analysis of surface waves. Shear wave velocity (Vs30)
Vertical electrical sounding of the subsurface for groundwater exploration
Seismic refraction profiling of shallow bedrock and the weathered zone
Reflection seismics using high-frequency P-wave sources for deep surveys
questions.solution: MASW: dispersion curve inversion. Vs30 for seismic site classification (NEHRP).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: En échelon tension gashes, sigmoidal arrays of quartz/calcite veins, are used in deformed rocks to determine:
options: Fault plane along which measurable slip has occurred during brittle deformation of the crust
Stylolite formed by pressure solution with seams of insoluble residue
Arrays of quartz/calcite veins. Sigmoidal shape = shear. Angle to shear direction → sense
Joint formed by tensile opening perpendicular to the least principal stress
questions.solution: Tension gashes: opening perpendicular to σ₃. Rotated with progressive shear.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which set of landforms characteristically develops in cold, non-glacial periglacial regions under intense freeze-thaw action?
options: Ridge of glaciofluvial sand and gravel deposited by a stream beneath a glacier
Patterned ground (sorted circles, polygons), pingos, ice wedges, solifluction lobes
Unsorted mixture of clay, sand and boulders deposited directly beneath or at the margin of a glacier
Layered sand and gravel washed out beyond the glacier snout by streams of glacial meltwater
questions.solution: Periglacial: freeze-thaw cycles. Permafrost (continuous, discontinuous). Pingos: ice-cored mound.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Granite classification — S, I, A, M types:
options: Explosive volcanic classification of igneous rocks based on silica content and the explosivity index of their eruptions
Division restricted to granodiorite and tonalite on the basis of modal quartz
Classification based only on the colour index and grain size of the rock
S (sedimentary source, peraluminous), I (igneous source, metaluminous), A (anorogenic, alkaline), M (mantle)
questions.solution: S-type: muscovite, monazite. I-type: hornblende, titanite. A-type: fluorite, high Ga/Al.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an aquifer, transmissivity equals the product of which two quantities, and what are its typical units?
options: Hydraulic conductivity multiplied by aquifer thickness
Storage coefficient multiplied by the saturated aquifer thickness
Effective porosity multiplied by aquifer thickness
Permeability divided by the aquifer's thickness
questions.solution: T = Kb. Units: m2/day.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Polymorph: same composition, different crystal structure:
options: Same structure. Polymorphs share an identical crystal structure but differ in chemical formula
Different minerals. Polymorphs have different compositions but identical crystal structures
Carbon: diamond (cubic) vs graphite (hexagonal). SiO₂: quartz vs coesite vs stishovite
Different composition. Polymorphs have the same structure but vary in elemental chemistry
questions.solution: Polymorph: diamond/graphite. Calcite/aragonite. Rutile/anatase/brookite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes a chevron fold from a concentric (parallel) fold in terms of limb shape and layer thickness?
options: Chevron: curved limbs maintaining constant layer thickness. Concentric: sharp angular hinge
Chevron: no defined hinge zone. Concentric: limb thickness increases toward the hinge
Chevron: rounded hinges with variable thickness. Concentric: strictly straight planar limbs
Chevron: straight limbs, sharp hinge. Concentric: constant layer thickness (parallel)
questions.solution: Chevron: similar folds. Concentric: parallel folds. Detachment folds above décollement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic wave velocities in Earth's layers:
options: All same. A uniform 8 km/s velocity applies to every shell from the crust to the inner core
Random and unpredictable, so no consistent velocity profile characterises the deep Earth
Crust: 6-7 km/s. Upper mantle: 8 km/s. Lower mantle: 13 km/s. Outer core: 8 km/s. Inner core: 11 km/s
Decrease with depth, so that the highest P-wave velocities occur in the crust and near-zero values in the inner core
questions.solution: P-wave velocity generally increases with depth. Drop at CMB (liquid outer core).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Birefringence of a mineral viewed under a microscope is defined as what?
options: Reflection of light from a mineral surface back to the eye
Degree to which a mineral absorbs light of a given wavelength
Product of refractive index and specific gravity of the mineral
questions.solution: Birefringence: n_epsilon - n_omega. Measured on universal stage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 3 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 5.73 (in the given time units). Its age is:
questions.solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 3×5.73 = 17.19.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Coastal erosion management: groynes work by:
options: Dissipating wave energy by breaking incoming waves
Reducing the tidal range through structural heightening
Adding artificial sediment to rebuild eroded beaches
questions.solution: Groynes: perpendicular structures trap sediment. Protect updrift side. Can cause downdrift erosion. Part of coastal defense.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 6 km/s and arrives 10 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 6×10 = 60 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tidal rhythmites in sedimentary successions record which periodic tidal process?
options: Storm surge events in a shallow basin
Seasonal runoff cycles in a glacial lake
questions.solution: Rhythmites: alternating thick-thin laminae. Record spring (thick) and neap (thin) tides. Used to calculate Earth-Moon distance.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sedimentary rocks, what do mud cracks formed in wet clay-rich sediment indicate, and how do they appear?
options: Desiccation cracks formed in loose aeolian dune sand. Rounded and hemispherical
Cracks formed by rapid cooling of hot volcanic lava flows. Columnar jointing pattern
Desiccation cracks in wet sediment. Polygonal. Top of bed indicator
Desiccation cracks formed by thermal contraction in frozen permafrost ground. Only in glacial till
questions.solution: Mud cracks: form by drying. Filled by overlying sediment.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 25 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A basal pinacoid, a simple crystal form, consists of how many parallel faces?
questions.solution: Pinacoid: {001} — two parallel faces. Closed form when combined with other forms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gravity survey: Bouguer anomaly correction for terrain:
options: Corrects for elevation of station above datum only
Accounts for gravitational effect of topography around station
Removes the regional variation due to latitude and rotation
Cancels the gravitational attraction of the Earth's mantle entirely
questions.solution: Terrain: mass correction for hills/valleys. Spherical cap or prism integration.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which intrusive igneous body is concordant and domes the overlying strata?
options: Concordant intrusion that domes overlying strata
Discordant intrusion that cross-cuts the enclosing country rocks
Concordant intrusion that forms broad flat layers of basaltic composition
Narrow cylindrical body filling the feeder conduit of a volcano
questions.solution: Laccolith: mushroom-shaped. Overlying beds arched upward.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness of orthoclase feldspar on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Orthoclase (KAlSi3O8) — hardness 6. Two good cleavages at 90°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement comparing the cooling and grain size of granite and basalt is INCORRECT?
options: Basalt is a fine-grained extrusive rock that forms from rapidly cooled lava
Granite cools faster than basalt, giving it finer grains
Granite is a coarse-grained intrusive rock composed largely of quartz and feldspar
Slow cooling of magma at depth allows the growth of large interlocking crystals
questions.solution: Granite cools slowly at depth (coarse grains); basalt cools fast at the surface (fine grains) — the claim is reversed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Molluscan shells are composed of which carbonate minerals, and which mineral group is generally absent?
options: Shells are predominantly composed of silica (opal), with calcite restricted to the hinge region
All shells are built of pure calcite, and aragonite never occurs in any mollusc group
Aragonite (most), calcite (some), both (some). Not silica (except in diatoms)
Shell mineralogy is fixed within each class and never mixes calcite with aragonite layers
questions.solution: Molluscs: aragonite common. Bivalves: aragonite or calcite. Gastropods: aragonite. Cephalopods: aragonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Blueschist facies: key mineral glaucophane:
options: Green Ca-amphibole (hornblende). Stable at moderate P and T
Black Fe-amphibole. Characteristic of contact aureoles
White K-mica. Diagnostic of Barrovian metamorphic zones
Blue Na-amphibole. Stable at high P, low T (subduction)
questions.solution: Glaucophane: Na₂(Mg₃Al₂)Si₈O₂₂(OH)₂. Blue color. Subduction zone metamorphism.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a highly vesicular felsic volcanic glass that floats on water?
options: Frothy basaltic lava that forms brittle cinder cones around vents
Highly vesicular felsic volcanic glass (floats on water)
Dense volcanic rock formed by slow crystallization of gabbroic magma
Vitreous aphanitic rock produced by quenching of rhyolitic melt
questions.solution: Pumice: abundant gas bubbles. Used as lightweight aggregate, abrasive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In slope stability analysis, the factor of safety is calculated as:
options: FS = driving force/resisting force. FS < 1 for a stable, safe slope
FS = c + σ·tanφ, independent of slope height and groundwater conditions
FS = 2.0 always; higher values mean the slope will fail immediately
questions.solution: FS = (c·L + W·cosθ·tanφ)/(W·sinθ). Limit equilibrium methods (Bishop, Janbu).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Satellite sensor spatial resolution: Landsat vs Sentinel-2 vs high-res (WorldView):
questions.solution: Landsat: 30m (multispectral), 15m (pan). Sentinel-2: 10m. WorldView: 0.31m (pan), 1.24m (MS).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: NDVI range: -1 to +1. Water bodies typically have NDVI:
options: Near +1, as water is very reflective
questions.solution: Water: low NIR reflectance, negative NDVI. Vegetation: 0.6-0.9. Bare soil: 0.1-0.2.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS-based hydrological modeling, what processing of a DEM is required to derive flow accumulation, stream networks, and watersheds?
options: Flow accumulation and watershed delineation can be run on an unfilled DEM directly
Stream network extraction requires only slope; sink filling is optional preprocessing
Flow accumulation, stream network, watershed delineation. Sink filling required
Watershed boundaries are derived from aspect alone, without flow direction grids
questions.solution: DEM → fill sinks → flow direction (D8) → flow accumulation → stream threshold → watershed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Web GIS: WMS (Web Map Service) vs WFS (Web Feature Service):
options: WMS: rendered images. WFS: vector features (editable)
WMS: delivers vector features. WFS: rendered raster images
WMS: raster only. WFS: raster only, with editing enabled
WMS and WFS both deliver vector features over the HTTP protocol
questions.solution: WMS: map images (PNG). WFS: GML/GeoJSON features. WCS: coverage (raster data).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing system uses an active sensor operating in the microwave region and can image at night as well as through cloud cover?
options: A passive sensor recording natural microwave emissions from the Earth surface
An optical sensor that is limited to daytime use and cloud-free conditions
Active sensor. Day/night, cloud penetration. SAR: synthetic aperture
A thermal sensor that measures emitted longwave radiation during the night
questions.solution: Radar: transmits pulses. Backscatter depends on roughness, moisture, geometry. Interferometry.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geological conditions are most important when selecting a dam site?
options: Foundation on thick alluvial gravel with a high seepage gradient below
Uniform flat-lying shale beds with a weak shear zone along the foundation
Foundation on competent rock, watertight abutments, no active faults
Reservoir site underlain by soluble gypsum and anhydrite formations
questions.solution: Dam: avoid karst (leakage), shears, soluble rocks. Grout curtain for seepage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which silica-undersaturated felsic plutonic rock contains nepheline instead of quartz?
options: Mafic plutonic rock dominated by olivine and pyroxene with accessory chromite
Silica-oversaturated rock consisting essentially of quartz and K-feldspar
Felsic plutonic with nepheline instead of quartz. Silica-undersaturated
Alkaline volcanic rock composed mainly of leucite and sanidine phenocrysts
questions.solution: Nepheline syenite: nepheline replaces quartz. No free SiO2. Alkaline suite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the undisturbed stratigraphic column shown (top to base: A, B, C, D), the oldest layer is:
questions.solution: By the law of superposition, the lowest bed (D) is the oldest in an undisturbed sequence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which textural features and sedimentary structures characterize the deposits of the beach and shoreface facies?
options: Poorly sorted, matrix-supported gravel deposited by high-density debris flows
Well-sorted, rounded, laminated sand. Swash and trough cross-bedding
Rounded, gravel-sized clasts with imbrication and no internal stratification at all
Laminated mud with flaser bedding and abundant marine bioturbation throughout the unit
questions.solution: Beach: high energy. Heavy mineral placers (ilmenite, garnet, magnetite).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sequence lists the Barrovian index minerals in order of increasing metamorphic grade?
questions.solution: Index minerals indicate metamorphic grade. Each stable in specific P-T window.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR): frequency vs depth:
options: Lower frequencies give finer resolution while higher frequencies always penetrate deeper
Higher frequency (500MHz): higher resolution, shallower. Lower (50MHz): deeper, lower resolution
Penetration depth is governed solely by antenna size and not by operating frequency
Higher frequencies penetrate much deeper than low frequencies because they are less attenuated by wet clay soils
questions.solution: GPR: 10-2000 MHz. Depth: 1m (500MHz) to 50m (25MHz). Resolution: λ/4.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Placer deposits form by the concentration of heavy minerals through which agents?
options: Chemical precipitation of sulfides from metal-rich hydrothermal springs
Concentration of light minerals such as quartz and feldspar in beach sands
Biogenic accumulation of carbonates and siliceous tests on the deep sea floor by planktonic organisms
Heavy mineral concentration by water/wind. Gold, tin, diamond, ilmenite, zircon
questions.solution: Placer: alluvial, beach, eluvial, paleoplacer. Black sand: ilmenite + magnetite. Witwatersrand gold.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating of quartz or feldspar gives the time since the mineral was last exposed to what?
options: Applicable to any age range and any mineral type without any restriction at all
Quartz/feldspar. Last exposure to sunlight → burial age. Range ~100-200ka
Works only on carbon-bearing organic materials of a recent age and origin
Requires continuous sunlight during the laboratory measurement of the sample
questions.solution: OSL: quartz OSL (blue light stimulation). IRSL: feldspar (IR stimulation). SAR protocol.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the Von Mises yield criterion, plastic deformation begins when the deviatoric stress components satisfy which condition?
options: Yielding occurs when the maximum principal stress reaches the uniaxial yield strength σ_y
Yielding when the maximum shear stress equals half the tensile yield strength in a tension test
Yielding occurs when total strain energy per unit volume attains a critical threshold value
questions.solution: Von Mises: equivalent stress σ_eq = √((σ₁-σ₂)²+(σ₂-σ₃)²+(σ₃-σ₁)²)/√2.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 30 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 30/15 = 2 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 10 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The Darcy velocity is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, what hardness value does the mineral corundum have?
questions.solution: Corundum (Al2O3) — 9. Sapphire and ruby are gem varieties.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a playa lake and its deposits in an arid basin?
options: Permanent freshwater lake formed in a tectonically subsiding rift valley
Deep stratified lake with oxygen-depleted bottom waters and varved sediments
Temporary lake in arid basin. Evaporite deposits. Salt crust
Inland sea of perennial water connected to the ocean through a river channel
questions.solution: Playa: sabkha (coastal). Ephemeral. Evaporite minerals: halite, gypsum, borax.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI):
questions.solution: NDWI: McFeeters (1996). Positive values = water. MNDWI: uses SWIR instead of NIR.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a major geological hazard associated with dam reservoirs?
options: Uniform uplift of the foundation caused by thawing of frozen valley slopes
Total elimination of groundwater recharge in the entire downstream valley
Only thermal expansion of the dam crest concrete during summer months
questions.solution: RIS: impoundment triggers small quakes. Koyna (M6.3, 1967). Induced seismicity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Boninite: high-Mg, high-Si volcanic rock. Tectonic setting:
options: Mid-ocean ridge spreading centre with depleted MORB production
Intraplate hot spot chain culminating in a mantle plume axis
Continental rift valley filled with alkaline basalt flows and tuffs
questions.solution: Boninite: MgO>8%, SiO₂>52%, TiO₂<0.5%. Forearc setting. High-T partial melting of hydrated mantle.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Indian Stratigraphy: Vindhyan Supergroup age:
options: Cenozoic (~66 Ma to present). Deccan-related platform covers
Proterozoic (~1.6-0.6 Ga). Older and younger Vindhyan
Mesozoic (~251-66 Ma). Continental coal-bearing Gondwana sediments
Archean (~4.0-2.5 Ga). Basement gneisses and greenstone belts
questions.solution: Vindhyan: Semri, Kaimur, Rewa, Bhander groups. ~1.6 Ga to ~0.6 Ga.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sedimentary rocks, what distinguishes a breccia from a conglomerate by the shape of its clasts?
options: Well-rounded, well-sorted clasts cemented by calcite and silica
Clay-sized particles that split into thin fissile layers along bedding
Evaporite minerals precipitated directly from a supersaturated brine
questions.solution: Breccia: angular fragments. Near-source deposition (fault zones, talus).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Eclogite to granulite transition (decompression):
options: Complete melting of the assemblage to form a granitic melt
questions.solution: Decompression: omphacite → low-Na Cpx + Pl (symplectite). Garnet → Opx + Pl + Sp.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 30 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×30 = 240 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Laterite nickel deposits form primarily through which geological process?
options: Tropical weathering of ultramafic rocks concentrating Ni
Hydrothermal replacement of carbonate country rocks adjacent to granitic intrusions
Volcanic exhalation of metal-rich brines onto the Precambrian sea floor
Glacial plucking and ice-borne transport of chromite grains into terminal moraines
questions.solution: Laterite: tropical weathering enriches Ni and Co.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Re-Os dating, based on the beta decay of ¹⁸⁷Re to ¹⁸⁷Os, is most commonly applied to which geological materials?
options: ¹⁸⁷Re → ¹⁸⁷Os (β⁻). T½ = 41.6 Ga. For sulfides, black shale, oil. Mantle vs crust signature
K-Ar method applied to potassium-bearing silicate minerals and glass of the rock
¹⁴⁷Sm → ¹⁴³Nd (α). T½ = 106 Ga. Applied to mafic and ultramafic rocks, REE minerals and their whole rocks
U-Pb method applied to zircon and other uranium-bearing minerals in the rock
questions.solution: Re-Os: direct dating of ore minerals. Orogenic gold, VMS. Mantle: ¹⁸⁷Os/¹⁸⁸Os ~0.13.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the typical architecture of a fault zone, from the fault core outward to the undeformed wall rock?
options: Core zone is the widest part, with damage zone confined to a single narrow fracture band
Damage zone has the lowest permeability and protolith shows the most intense fracturing
A single fracture surface separates two undeformed wall-rock blocks with no damage at all
questions.solution: Fault core: ≤10% of zone width. Damage zone: increased fracture density. Permeability barrier/conduit.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 50000 m² has 30 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 50000×30 = 1500000 m³ = 1.5 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The colour of a mineral's powder, seen when it is rubbed on a porcelain plate, is its:
questions.solution: Streak is the colour of the fine powder, often more diagnostic than the surface colour.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Remote sensing of mineralogy: ASTER bands for hydrothermal alteration:
options: SWIR bands (5,6,7,8) for clay, carbonate, sericite
VNIR bands (1,2,3) for iron oxide and hematite mapping
TIR bands (10-14) for iron and manganese oxides only
Single SWIR band 8 for all alteration minerals
questions.solution: ASTER SWIR: clay (band 6), carbonate (band 8), alunite (band 5). OH absorption features.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What term describes a large (>100 km²), discordant intrusive igneous body?
options: Concordant body smaller than 100 km², with domed roof, emplaced along bedding
Small discordant plug occupying the throat of an ancient volcano
Large intrusive igneous body (>100 km²), discordant
Volcanic cone built entirely of alternating lava flows and pyroclastic layers
questions.solution: Batholith: massive granitic intrusion. Root of mountain belts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which transformation occurs between anhydrite and gypsum near the Earth's surface?
options: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) converts to anhydrite (CaSO4) by gaining water during shallow burial near the surface
Anhydrite (CaSO₄) dehydrates to gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) near surface. Volume increase ~30%
Anhydrite (CaSO4) and gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) are polymorphs unrelated by any hydration or dehydration reaction
Anhydrite (CaSO4) loses water to become gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) at depth, with a volume decrease of about 30%
questions.solution: Anhydrite: deeper, hotter. Gypsum: near surface. Gypsification: volume increase, expansion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the gravity method, the Bouguer anomaly is obtained by applying which corrections and slab term to the observed gravity?
options: Difference between observed gravity and the gravity predicted for a uniform reference ellipsoid
Measured gravity reduced for elevation but leaving slab and terrain uncorrected
Gravity effect of the compensating mass required by the crustal root at depth
Observed gravity — latitude correction — free-air — Bouguer slab + terrain. Δg_B = 2πGρh
questions.solution: Bouguer: density variations in crust. Regional (deep) + residual (shallow). Microgravity: cavities.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 50 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which radar technique compares the phase difference between two SAR images of the same area to detect ground deformation?
options: Amplitude difference between two images for feature classification
Phase difference between two images. Measures cm-scale deformation
Doppler shift of a single image to measure target velocity
Coherence loss only, giving no quantitative displacement data
questions.solution: InSAR: DEM (topography) and DInSAR (displacement). Atmospheric artifacts. Persistent scatterers.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Diagenetic zone of sandstone — mesogenesis:
options: Near-surface weathering zone with intense dissolution, karst porosity and vadose cementation only
Moderate burial (1-4 km). Quartz overgrowths, pressure solution, carbonate cement
Extreme burial beyond 10 km with recrystallization, schistosity and partial melting of framework grains
Zone of contact metamorphism adjacent to igneous intrusions where new minerals grow along grain contacts
questions.solution: Mesogenesis: mechanical compaction → chemical compaction. Primary porosity loss.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which optical property of a mineral is described by the term diaphaneity?
options: Way light reflects off the surface
questions.solution: Transparent (light passes), translucent (light diffused), opaque (no light).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In stratigraphic correlation, which of the following rock units or features serve as reliable marker beds?
options: Volcanic ash (bentonite), marine transgression, iridium anomaly, magnetic reversal
Beds of similar colour, thickness and grain size in nearby sections of the same basin
Thick conglomerate and breccia beds at the base of every basin fill deposit
The thickest and most persistent sandstone unit within a given basin succession
questions.solution: Bentonite: volcanic ash. Key: widespread, thin, distinct. Iridium: K-Pg boundary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which structural group of silicates does the feldspar group of minerals belong?
questions.solution: Feldspars: orthoclase (K-spar), plagioclase (Na-Ca). Most abundant crustal mineral.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: For a geological cross-section to be considered balanced, what condition must be satisfied during restoration?
options: Conservation of bed length alone, ignoring any changes in the area of individual layers
Uniform horizontal shortening applied equally to every layer in the section without pinning
Conservation of bed length and area during restoration
Restoration with gap formation permitted in the synclines and fold crests of the section
questions.solution: Balanced: no gaps or overlaps after restoration. Bed length and area preserved.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In Ramsay's fold classification, Classes 1, 2 and 3 are distinguished on the basis of which feature?
options: Class 1: dip isogons diverge outward. Class 2: isogons strictly parallel. Class 3: isogons converge inward
Class 1: layers thicken on the limbs. Class 2: constant thickness. Class 3: thicken at the hinge
Class 1: no thickness change. Class 2: limb thickening. Class 3: thickening everywhere
Class 1: dip isogons converge inward. Class 2: parallel (similar). Class 3: converge outward
questions.solution: Ramsay: based on layer thickness and curvature. Class 1A: thickened at hinge. 1B: parallel (concentric).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The section shows 20 m of overburden above a 4 m coal seam. The volumetric stripping ratio (overburden : coal thickness) is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 20/4 = 5 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do braided and meandering river channel patterns differ with respect to sediment load, discharge, and channel stability?
options: Meandering channels develop only where the river maintains a very steep valley gradient
Braided and meandering channel patterns develop under identical hydraulic and sediment conditions
Braided channels occur where the river carries very little bedload and discharge is steady
Braided: high sediment load, variable discharge. Meandering: stable, fine sediment
questions.solution: Braided: high energy, coarse sediment. Meandering: lower energy, fine sediment, cohesive banks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the channel morphology and bank features of a meandering river?
options: Single straight channel with uniform width and no lateral migration
Single channel, sinuous. Cut bank (outer) + point bar (inner). Scroll bars
Multiple channels that split and rejoin around bars, with high sediment load and variable discharge
Straight single channel with uniform width, no lateral migration and no point bars
questions.solution: Meander: sinuosity > 1.5. Meander wavelength: 10-14× channel width. Neck vs chute cutoff.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 50 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The Darcy velocity is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+25+10) = 61%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a conjugate joint system, the two joint sets intersect parallel to which principal stress direction?
options: The intermediate principal stress direction σ₂
The maximum principal compressive stress direction σ₁ at the time of joint formation
The minimum principal stress direction σ₃, along which opening joints normally develop
The resultant of σ₁ and σ₃, bisecting the acute angle between the two joint sets
questions.solution: Conjugate shear joints: intersection lineation = σ₂. Acute bisector = σ₁.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to Bowen's reaction series, mineral crystallization proceeds through which two types of reaction series?
options: A single uninterrupted reaction series in which all minerals crystallize in a fixed order from the melt
A series in which every mineral melts rather than crystallizes upon cooling
A discontinuous series limited only to quartz-bearing granitic magmas
questions.solution: Early crystals: olivine, Ca-plagioclase. Late: quartz, K-feldspar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: When water seeps under a dam, the exit gradient must be safe, because an unsafe value leads to:
options: Seepage is always negligible for well-compacted clay cores
Exit gradient must be safe (< critical gradient). Piping failure
Seepage stops once the reservoir reaches a steady water level
Seepage below the dam reduces the uplift pressure on its foundation
questions.solution: Critical gradient i_c = (G_s-1)/(1+e). Piping: backward erosion. Filter design to prevent.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement about anticlines is correct?
options: The youngest beds lie in the core of an anticline
The oldest beds lie in the core of an anticline
An anticline is a downward fold
questions.solution: Erosion of an upfold exposes the oldest strata at its core; anticlines are classic hydrocarbon traps.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the seismic reflection method, subsurface structure is imaged using which waves and processing steps such as CMP stacking and migration?
options: Mapping of the subsurface using critically refracted first arrivals at long offsets
Determination of the water table using direct current injected through steel electrodes
Estimation of rock density contrasts from measurement of the Earth's gravity field at the surface
Subsurface imaging by reflected P-waves. CMP stacking, migration. Resolution: λ/4 (~20m at 50 Hz)
questions.solution: Reflection: petroleum exploration. 2D, 3D seismic. Vibroseis (land), airgun (marine).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Flinn diagram: K = (R-1)/(R-1) where R = axial ratios. K>1 indicates:
options: Oblate (pancake-shaped) fabric indicating that flattening strain is dominant over elongation
Plane strain in which the intermediate principal strain axis is not deformed
Flattening strain with the greatest shortening along the maximum principal stress direction
questions.solution: K>1: elongation dominant (L-tectonite). K<1: flattening dominant (S-tectonite). K=1: plane strain.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Carbonate grain types: ooids, peloids, bioclasts, intraclasts. Ooids form in:
options: Cold, deep oceanic water far below the carbonate compensation depth
Glacial meltwater streams carrying suspended carbonate silt into fjords
Warm, shallow, agitated marine water (high energy)
Shallow, calm lagoonal water with abundant algae and low salinity
questions.solution: Ooids: spherical, concentric layers. Form in warm, shallow, agitated water. Bahama Banks type.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Under which conditions do kink bands typically form in strongly foliated rocks?
options: Strongly foliated rocks under compressive stress parallel to foliation
Isotropic massive rocks under equal hydrostatic confining pressure applied in all directions
Unfoliated coarse-grained plutonic rocks subjected to low-grade retrograde metamorphism
Homogeneous rocks deformed by pure tension acting normal to the future fold axial plane
questions.solution: Kink bands: angular folds in well-foliated rocks. Foliation rotates sharply across kink band.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits, formed by submarine volcanic exhalative activity, are enriched in which metals?
options: Lateritic enrichment of nickel and cobalt by intense tropical chemical weathering
Sedimentary exhalation of Zn-Pb-Ag brines into reducing anoxic rift basin waters on the ancient seafloor
Mechanical concentration of heavy resistant minerals by fluvial and beach processes
Cu-Zn-Pb ± Au-Ag. Submarine volcanic exhalative. Kuroko (Japan), Noranda, Kidd Creek
questions.solution: VMS: stratiform, lens-shaped. Stringer zone (feeder) + massive ore. Besshi, Cyprus, Kuroko types.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A migmatite rock is the product of which process of metamorphism?
options: Complete melting followed by magma crystallization
Shallow burial diagenesis of a sedimentary unit
Injection of an unrelated granitic intrusion
questions.solution: Migamatite: mixed rock (leucosome + melanosome). Represents partial melting at deep crustal levels. Transition to igneous.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 0.7 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 0.7 Gyr (equal to one full half-life of the parent)
questions.solution: 50% remaining ⇒ 1 half-lives ⇒ age = 1×0.7 = 0.7 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are tsunamis most commonly generated, and at what magnitude do thrust-fault earthquakes trigger them?
options: Ocean wave from underwater earthquake (M>7, thrust fault). Velocity ~√(gh)
Giant tidal wave caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun only
Slow surface current driven by wind and the Earth's rotation alone
Local storm surge generated by cyclonic winds blowing over the open sea
questions.solution: Tsunami: long wavelength (>100 km). Wave height increases in shallow water. Run-up.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Under what conditions does hummocky cross-stratification (HCS) typically form in marine sediments?
options: Formed by tidal currents in a shallow estuary. Bipolar foresets with mud drapes
Formed by storm waves below fair-weather wave base. Undulating sets, low angle
Formed by oscillatory waves above fair-weather wave base in a high-energy foreshore
Formed by unidirectional turbidity currents on the continental slope. Sole marks present
questions.solution: HCS: diagnostic of storm-dominated shelves. Hummocks: 3D cross-sets. Swales: concave down.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The compound eyes of trilobites are unique among arthropods because they are made of what mineral?
options: Aragonite prisms arranged in a simple lens array
Silica spicules that form a single large biconvex lens
Chitinous lenses lacking any mineral reinforcement
questions.solution: Trilobite eyes: calcite lenses. Holochroal (many lenses) or schizochroal (fewer, larger lenses).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock body that can store and transmit usable amounts of groundwater is a(n):
questions.solution: An aquifer is porous and permeable enough to yield water to wells.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gas content of a coal seam is commonly measured in the laboratory using which method?
options: Desorption canister method. Measure gas released over time, extrapolate to total gas
Downhole geophysical logging of coal beds to estimate gas pressure and saturation trends
Seismic refraction profiling of the seam to infer zones of high gas content
Direct drilling of the seam followed by open-hole permeability testing only
questions.solution: Canister: sealed coal sample, measure desorbed gas. Extrapolate using √t or diffusion model.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In porphyry copper systems, alteration zones from the center outward follow which sequence?
options: Sodic-calcic alteration confined to the surrounding metamorphic aureole, absent inside the intrusion
Potassic (center) → phyllic → argillic → propylitic (outer). Sericite, chlorite, clay
A single quartz-sericite zone enveloping the entire stockwork vein system
Irregular distribution controlled solely by the fracture density of the host rock
questions.solution: Porphyry: Cu-Mo. Low grade (0.3-1% Cu). Large tonnage. Stockwork veins. Chile, USA, Indonesia.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In thin section, how does biotite typically display pleochroism?
options: Weak — pale grey with no visible color change
Absent — biotite is isotropic under crossed polars
Strong — dark brown to pale yellow (brown mineral)
Red to green with strong variation in both axes
questions.solution: Biotite: strong pleochroism. One cleavage direction. 'Bird's eye' extinction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Biostratigraphic zone: range zone defined by:
options: The most abundant fossil species in a local measured column
A dated volcanic ash bed that caps the local succession
The last appearance of a fossil genus in a measured section
First and last appearance of index fossil
questions.solution: Range zone: FAD to LAD of index fossil. Assemblage zone: characteristic assemblage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Oxide copper resources are most amenable to which processing method?
options: Direct smelting of the carbonate-hosted oxide ore
Gravity tabling of dense malachite and cuprite grains
Dry magnetic separation of the ferruginous oxide fraction
questions.solution: Oxide Cu: soluble in sulfuric acid. Heap leach or in-situ.
